assets.hurdle-stride.png:
Use case: illustration-story / animation production. A clean HORIZONTAL landscape, 3 columns by 2 rows character ANIMATION EXPOSURE SHEET for a single low track hurdle jump. EXACTLY SIX complete, separate full-body cels; no panels, text, guides, labels, numbers, shadows, ground, props or scenery. True transparent background. Image 1 is the exact silver/turquoise athletic robot AND model proportions. Image 2 is its established hurdle silhouette. Image 3 shows the installed tiny lavender lidar puck, blue ear camera and small amber chest sensor; draw them on EACH cel, as well as a discrete pale mint sole strip. Keep the same black visor with one visible cyan eye, friendly expression, graphite joints, crisp weight-varied ink and turquoise / cool silver cel shading. SAME head size, bone lengths, camera looking straight at its left side, running toward the RIGHT in every cell. Two leg silhouettes are distinct; near limb lighter, far limb slightly darker. Use genuine athlete hurdling mechanics and opposite arm drive. Six independent images in equal cells, each fully inside its own cell with generous transparent gutter and margin, nothing touching or cropped. Do not encode the parabolic arc as layout: each character centered in its own cell. Read left-to-right top-to-bottom:
1 Last stride into the plant. Front foot planted nearly below the hip, rear heel kicking toward the backside, slight forward lean, hips moderately flexed.
2 TOE-OFF. Planting leg extended long behind and pressing the ground only with its toe, heel raised. Opposite knee drives forward and up with its shin folded back; opposite arm drives forward.
3 RISING: forward knee now higher than hip and beginning to open, foot moves out in front, trail heel folds behind, torso drives forward. Distinct from 2.
4 CLEARANCE: iconic horizontal hurdler at apex from image 2, long lead leg extended to the RIGHT with its toe raised, rear leg bent and tucked back, torso inclines over lead thigh, one arm reaches ahead. Actual athlete jumping FORWARD with separated legs.
5 DESCENDING: lead leg swings DOWN to meet the track UNDER and slightly ahead of hips, ball of lead foot points down, trail knee advances flexed, torso lifts.
6 TOUCHDOWN: just the lead foot planted, receiving knee bends to absorb weight, rear foot is airborne and swinging through high, natural opposite arm. Avoid squatting, lunging with both feet on floor, hands on knees, or legs crossed unnaturally. One connected intact robot per cel. The six drawings should be suitable for a professional hand-drawn inbetween animator.

TOP RIGHT short passing position, near flat support directly UNDER hips, far flexed knee moving forward past it with its foot lifted. BOTTOM LEFT far/darker leg now reaches forward and supports; near bright leg visibly trails back, lifted heel; switch the arm swing. BOTTOM RIGHT other passing position, the far leg carries weight under hips, the near bright knee is now advancing with toe lifted. Arms bent, elbows close to ribs, pumping. Silhouettes should read as an athlete stepping in a low posture, keeping low and moving decisively forward with both knees well above the soles.
